title: I Made the Group Project Portal Show Who Typed Nothing

parts.text: I exported the Google Doc version history at 11:52 p.m. and watched my name do all the typing. I am nineteen, broke freshman, desperate for the lab grade. Our group chat was named no stress!! which was a lie. Tyler sent memes. Aisha sent, "I'll do slides tomorrow." Tomorrow was three tomorrows ago. The TA, Ben, had said contribution would be even. The doc smelled like panic if docs could smell. I had a mug of gas-station coffee, metallic and wrong. Tyler zoomed in from a dark dorm. "Just submit. We'll split credit." I said, "You wrote twelve words." He laughed. "Vibes are work." Aisha did not join the call. I pasted the version history into an email draft to Ben, then didn't send it because I am nineteen and still think mercy is a strategy. At 12:10 Tyler submitted the file from his account so it would look like he owned it. The portal showed submitter: T. Nash. My figures, his name. I sat on the floor. The RA walked past, smelled the coffee, made a face. Then Ben posted a midnight announcement: submitters must attach a contribution note or the whole group gets a zero. Tyler pinged me, suddenly awake. "Write that I led." I stared at the blinking cursor in the portal. The contribution box had 500 characters. He wanted all of them to be a fiction with my fingerprints.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The portal wants a contribution note, he submitted under his name, and he wants me to write that he led.

social.video_title: He submitted my lab under his account — Part 1/2
social.description: Gas-station coffee, a chat named no stress, and version history that could not meme. The TA changed the rules at midnight. Would you have typed the fiction?

parts.text: I wrote the truth in 482 characters with timestamps. Tyler called me a snitch in the chat. Aisha finally appeared: "I didn't know." The history showed she didn't. Ben emailed us separately. Tyler got a zero for contribution and a meeting. I got the grade my figures earned. Aisha got a smaller penalty and a second chance. Tyler told the floor I was obsessed with credit. The RA, who had smelled my coffee, said obsession is how labs exist. I switched groups next unit. I still use version history like a religion. Tyler asked me to "be cool" before the final. I said cool is twelve words. He did his own figures, badly, and passed, which is allowed. I threw away the metallic coffee habit and bought a cheap kettle. Sometimes I open the old doc to remember that portals can be honest if you feed them honest notes. I am still broke. I am less merciful in group chats named with exclamation points. That is an education too. The cheap light over the sink flickered twice like punctuation I did not ask for.
